clue.text: Piggy banks good girl emptied for change?

indicators.note: to bank something is to hold it safely, so the piggy keeps the other letters within it

parts.note: 'this little piggy' is the nursery-rhyme name for a toe

indicators.note: a word emptied loses its contents, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A child's piggy bank is raided by a well-behaved girl looking for small coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piggy' looks like the money box, but it is the toe of the nursery rhyme; 'emptied' keeps only the outside of girl, giving GL.
explanation.definitionFit: To toggle is to switch between two states, a kind of change; the question mark flags the less obvious sense.

clue.text: What KFC doesn't have following mixed buffet?

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the abbreviation is left without one of its letters

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A fast-food chain is compared with an all-you-can-eat buffet that offers a mixture of dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: KFC without F is KC; 'mixed' scrambles WHAT and KC. 'Buffet' reads as a meal but is the verb, to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To buffet is to strike repeatedly, and a thwack is a sharp blow.

clue.text: Weed — reason tree is cut

parts.note: grounds are the reason or justification for something

indicators.note: the tree loses its tail end, as if cut short

parts.note: the elm is a common tree

explanation.surface: A gardener explains that a weed is the reason a tree had to be felled.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common yellow-flowered weed of gardens and waste ground.

clue.text: Island where monk shelters friend

indicators.note: to shelter is to hold within, so the friend goes inside the monk

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A monk on a remote island gives refuge to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: La Palma is one of the Canary Islands, in the Atlantic off Africa.

clue.text: Children boarding rather swift ship

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so these letters go into the other word

parts.note: sooner means rather, as in 'I'd sooner stay'

explanation.surface: Children climb aboard a rather fast sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rather' looks like it qualifies 'swift', but it supplies SOONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel prized for its speed.

clue.text: Left cutting remark in personal manner

indicators.note: cutting into means going inside, so the left side sits within the remark

parts.note: a comment is a remark
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone leaves after a cutting personal remark about their manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting remark' reads as a barb, but 'cutting' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Comportment is the way a person carries and conducts themselves, their bearing.

clue.text: Body of water connected with sailor I love

parts.note: on can mean connected with, as in 'on the subject'
tar is an old word for a sailor
love is nil in tennis, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A sailor declares his love for a stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Ontario is one of the North American Great Lakes.

clue.text: Liquid acid under new type of battery

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means placed after
liquid suggests something fluid and flowing, so the letters run into a new order

explanation.surface: A battery has fresh acid poured under it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid' rearranges ACID into ICAD, which goes under N.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicad is a rechargeable nickel-cadmium cell.

clue.text: On which toll booths would be most appropriate?

definitions.text: On which toll booths would be most appropriate?

parts.words: On which toll booths would be most appropriate?
parts.note: a toll is the sound of a bell ringing, so booths charging a toll suit a route whose name begins with what a bell does

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which highway would best suit toll booths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toll' is both a road charge and the sound of a bell, which rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road is a bypass circling a town; bells that toll also ring, hence the pun.

clue.text: Accepting work, that's my mistake

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the work goes inside

parts.note: that's can mean who's, as in 'the man that's here'
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone admits fault after taking on a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what one says on making a blunder, the same as saying 'my mistake'.

clue.text: Come on — it could be a symbol

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: An exhortation is shown as a typed symbol, perhaps a smiley.
explanation.definitionFit: An emoticon is a small typed picture such as a smiley face, a symbol of mood.

clue.text: Prison's a hindrance to an artist

parts.note: can is slang for prison
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A painter finds jail a hindrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prison's' joins CAN to the rest; LET as hindrance survives in tennis and the legal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was the eighteenth-century Venetian painter of city views.

clue.text: Unlikely — a diocese that has parts in Florida city

parts.note: tall means unlikely, as in a tall story

indicators.note: parts means separates, so the word has splits the other two

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: An unlikely claim that a diocese extends into a Florida city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlikely' gives TALL through the idea of a tall story, an unbelievable tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallahassee is the state capital of Florida.

clue.text: Jockey's personal requirements

definitions.meaning: a jockey is one who rides horses
a performer's contract may carry a list of personal demands added as a clause

explanation.surface: A jockey's personal needs are listed.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey is a horse rider, and a rider is an added contract clause listing a performer's demands.

clue.text: Katie clears throat — wrong answer

indicators.note: wrong signals the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Katie clears her throat before giving a wrong answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Gone with the Wind is christened Katie Scarlett, so Katie is her first given name.

clue.text: Metal blocks missing, evidently not tight

indicators.note: blocks means sits in the way, so the metal lodges inside the other word

parts.note: absent means missing
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Metal blocks have gone missing; clearly something is not tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk, so someone who abstains from drink is not tight.

clue.text: Treacherous fat cow's poorly educated

indicators.note: poorly suggests something badly put together, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An insult: a fat cow who is poorly educated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone two-faced is deceitful and disloyal, showing one face and hiding another.

clue.text: One may lose confidence if everything barber cuts is getting thinner

indicators.note: cuts means enters, so the inner words go into the outer

parts.note: fabric that wears is getting thinner with use
all means everything
to barber is to shave or trim someone

explanation.surface: A man fears losing confidence as his barber trims away hair already thinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barber' is a verb here and 'cuts' is the container signal; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns that you may be overheard, so a secret told in confidence may get out.

clue.text: 'Blind' is not a word to say

parts.note: sh is the call for silence, asking for not a word
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A warning that 'blind' is a word one must not say.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutter is a hinged window cover, a kind of blind.

clue.text: Get a group of singers on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers

explanation.surface: Someone tries to obtain a choir for a radio broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire is to obtain or come to possess something.

clue.text: Nothing's in code

definitions.meaning: a figure meaning zero or nought

explanation.surface: Nothing is hidden in a secret code.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means zero, nought, and also a coded message or secret writing system.

clue.text: Whenever turning cold, starts to hide under cape

indicators.note: turning signals the word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, I stay in'
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Whenever it turns cold, someone hides beneath a cape.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a small triangular shawl or cape worn round a woman's shoulders.

clue.text: Put a stop to France as Eurovision hosts

indicators.note: hosts means holds within, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: France should stop being the Eurovision host.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease something is to halt or end it.

clue.text: Relic from hostile desert? Yes, maybe

parts.note: anti means opposed or hostile
to desert is to quit
Y is the standard abbreviation for yes, as on forms

explanation.surface: A relic is found in a hostile desert, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' reads as sand dunes but is the verb, to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiquity is an object surviving from ancient times, a relic of the past.

clue.text: Appeal put around to have meeting about campaign for social reform

indicators.note: put around means wrapped outside, so the other letters go within

parts.note: charm is appeal or attractiveness

indicators.note: about signals a turn round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sit, as in sit-in, is a session or meeting

explanation.surface: Someone uses charm to arrange a meeting about a reform campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives TIS, and the 'meeting' sense of sit is the one in a sitting of a court or parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartism was the British working-class movement of the 1830s and 1840s demanding votes for all men.

clue.text: Space-age couple storing energy

indicators.note: storing means holding inside

parts.note: to hitch is to couple or join
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A futuristic couple keeps energy in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hi-tech uses advanced technology, like gadgets of the space age.

clue.text: Medic welcomes parent that is less attractive

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, a medic
to rear is to raise children, to parent them
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A doctor greets an unattractive parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Drearier means duller and gloomier, so less appealing.

clue.text: One funny way to interrupt abuse

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the way goes inside the abuse

parts.note: to jeer is to mock or abuse
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A comic interrupts heckling.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester was the court entertainer, someone paid to be comical.
